Universal apps make it easy to convert between desktop, phones, and tablets, but not web. ASP.NET is its own thing with very little in common with universal apps, and you don't want that server code on the phone anyway. You'd need to adapt the html and stuff that you see in a web browser, and doing that for an ASP.NET website is no easier than any other kind of website.

I'd agree for a non-database driven dynamic website. However, or something that's, presumably, as database driven as VOAT the ASP.NET is just interfacing (via C#) with the database to serve content. With new code for an app's front-end the libraries and resources should already be present for C# to interface with the database just as easily. That code is transferrable, and only aesthetic code, and maybe a few small semantic changes, should be needed to make the app work.

Allowing the mobile app to connect to the database directly would be a massive security flaw. Any user could decompile the app, grab the db creds, and wreak havoc. You need an API to serve as a middleman and validate everything, which last I heard is in beta.

If the code is written in C#, an API for access in C# would be complete already. Unless the web application (ASP.Net/C#) is connecting to the DB directly, and then we have, as you put it, havoc wreaking potential.

Pretty much every ASP.NET website, including this one, uses Entity Framework, which is just an ORM library. It's kind of an API, but it only checks for errors, not bad intent, so you can't use it to prevent people from doing bad things. Also it requires a username and password to be given to it in a connection string, so there's the security flaw.

That's why I was under the assumption that, if they had written from the ground up, they had used Entity in the beginning, but had worked in an API that allowed for connection to be handled off site. Is there at least a plan to remedy this in the future (i.e. once the API is complete). It's a pretty big security hole.
